articleTitle: Drive-cycle system efficiency evaluation of electrically excited synchronous machine with dynamic motor drive
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a method of drive-cycle system efficiency evaluation of the electrically excited synchronous machine (EESM) with dynamic motor drive is proposed. This method combines the finite elements analysis (FEA) in Ansys with the analytical method in Matlab. The system efficiency evaluation includes the power electronics, control strategy, electrical machine, and drive-cycle operation. The EESM employs the same stator structure and winding configuration as a commercial interior permanent magnet (IPM) machine and only its rotor is optimised by FEA. The torque, power, and efficiency of the optimised EESM are comprehensively compared with the IPM machine. It shows that the optimised EESM has higher torque, power, and system efficiency than the IPM machine.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast switching of GaN transistors for nanosecond-pulse generation using GaN HEMTs-based drivers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Due to smaller parasitic components such as a smaller gate charge, gallium nitride high-electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) can be used for applications that require ultra-fast switching including plasma generation, where the faster rise time of the applied high-voltage and high-current pulses leads to a more efficient yield. The gate driver circuit and its implementation mainly dominate the turn-on process of the GaN transistors. Therefore, this paper investigates two different gate drivers previously used for silicon and silicon carbide transistors, to reduce the turn-on time of GaN transistors. In the proposed methods, the switching performance of the main 650 V transistor has been evaluated in pulsed operation with a resistive load of 610 V and 107 A. The obtained rise time results for the single-IC and voltage-source gate drivers are 4.23 ns and 2.92 ns, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of an integrated EV on-board charger with a wide output voltage range
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces the design and implementation of a novel integrated on-board electric vehicle charger with a wide output voltage range. The work addresses the need for a universal integrated on-board battery charger that can charge batteries of different voltages for electric vehicles. The charger utilizes the existing traction inverter and motor to provide a charging function while eliminating the need for extra costly equipment. The 2.5kW charger consists of two stages: an AC/DC stage and a DC-DC stage. The AC/DC converter regulates the input voltage to a 400V DC output. The DC/DC stage executes buck and boost operations and provides a wide 200V- 800Voutput range accommodating present and future high-voltage batteries. The charger has a closed loop control strategy for the boost section that ensures a steady and regulated output and an open loop control approach for the buck for a simplified design. Through simulations in MATLAB/SIMULINK, the charger demonstrates effective voltage regulation in boost (800V) and buck (200V) modes with a peak-to-peak ripple within 1-2% of the nominal values. Further work involves constructing a physical prototype to validate the simulated results.

articleTitle: Interleaved dual buck converters with low current ripple for green hydrogen production
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, interleaved dual buck converters are analyzed for use with electrolyzers coupled to renewable energy sources. The topology offers advantages such as low blocking voltage stress, and the possibility to reach high current for large electrolyzers through interleaved connection of converter channels. Additionally, interleaved dual buck converters can generate points of current ripple cancellation for a discrete number of output voltage values, which increase as more channels are connected in interleaved mode. This can lead to a reduction in the power of each channel and extend the lifespan of the electrolyzer. The theoretical analysis of the converter and the dependence of the output current ripple on the different system variables and parameters are addressed. Simulation results are presented for a 6-channel interleaved configuration for a 1MWnominal power operating point, which can be reconfigured to 5 channels in order to reduce the output current ripple.

articleTitle: Development of a design tool using the Biot-Savart method for a novel air-cored HTS generator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Numerical modelling is an important approach for investigating the performance of superconducting generators, which show promise for competitive cost of energy in offshore wind turbine applications. In this work, we employed two methods to construct numerical models for a MW-class superconducting generator, featuring a rotor with high-temperature superconducting coils and a stator with conventional copper coils. The first method involves the Biot-Savart law in MATLAB to analysis the magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic force in the coils. Simultaneously, the second method utilizes the finite element analysis software COMSOL Multiphysics to create a 3D model for the generator. The simulation results of both methods show a reasonable agreement. The Biot-Savart method offers the advantage of extremely fast computation, while COMSOL provides versatility for 3D modelling with a quick modelling process.

articleTitle: Enhancing DC microgrids integration with three-phase AC grids using multiport converters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: DC microgrids offer a promising solution to meet the escalating demand for electric energy by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, energy storage, and loads. To enhance the stability and sustainability of DC microgrids, a bidirectional power interface with the utility grid is adopted. This paper proposes a non-isolated multiport converter that interfaces multiple DC microgrids with a three-phase AC grid, potentially allowing reductions of overall size and cost compared the multi-converter approach, and providing additional flexibility by allowing for a direct power exchange between the DC microgrids. The main objective of the study is to validate the superior performance of the proposed converter compared to the conventional approach of interconnecting DC-DC and AC-DC converters in a cascaded connection. The study comprehensively evaluates semiconductor device stresses, losses, total chip area, and magnetic element size for both approaches. Finally, experimental results of the proposed converter are presented.

articleTitle: A lifetime evaluation of SiC devices bonded with copper and silver sintering
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper compares two sintering materials currently in use for the manufacturing of power modules with compound semiconductors: silver and copper. The impact of the interconnection technology in the chip-near bonds is studied by comparing the number of cycles with a temperature rise of 130 °C achieved during power cycling according to the guidelines of the AQG-324 from the ECPE. SiC Schottky diode dies were used as the power devices, and they are compared against a discrete standard packaged device. The plots of junction temperature vs cycle number, and measured degradation are shown. Even though the silver-sintered devices failed earlier, they were able to carry twice the rated forward current. On the other hand, the coppersintered devices achieved a good current carrying capability, comparable junction-to-heatsink thermal resistance, and lasted over fifty thousand cycles.

articleTitle: Behaviour of modular multilevel DC/DC converter with DC voltage control integrated in a multi-terminal DC system under fault conditions
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The development of multi-terminal DC (MTDC) networks has various challenges as interconnecting grids of different voltages and grounding schemes, DC grid protection and power flow. DC/DC converter has emerged as the solution for interconnecting HVDC links with different specifications. In this paper, the front-to-front modular multilevel converter (F2F-MMC) topology is adopted for DC/DC converter, which can act as a firewall between the healthy and faulty grid during DC faults. Along with this, DC/DC converters when operated in DC voltage control mode can provide supplementary functionalities such as participating in DC grid voltage management and increasing the reliability of the system. In this study, the F2F-MMC converter is operated with a virtual resistance DC voltage controller integrated into an MTDC system. A pole-to-pole DC fault is applied on the MTDC grid and the influence of the virtual resistance controller associated with the DC/DC converter is studied for re-establishing the power flow after DC faults.

articleTitle: Reduced order model of a flywheel energy storage system for efficient electromagnetic transient simulation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a reduced flywheel energy storage system (FESS) model for efficient EMT-Type simulation in developed in the PSCAD simulation environment. The developed model considers an average value converter model for the grid side converter while a first order model representation of the flywheel is used for the machine side. The developed reduced model preserves speed and dc link voltage regulation, usually only considered in a detailed flywheel model, allowing the tracking of the FESS state of charge. The origin of minor discrepancies observed between results obtained with the reduced and detailed FESS models are also discussed. The gains brought by the simplistic FESS representation, in terms of computing efficiency and numerical stability for long time-steps, is assessed by comparing simulation results with a detailed implementation of a FESS in a time-restricted environment.

articleTitle: A combined three-phase AC boost rectifier and DC-DC converter based on dual three-phase machine drive for integrated battery charger of electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated battery charger for electric vehicles (EVs) that uses dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive as three-phase AC boost rectifier and DC-DC buck converter. The hardware circuit is arranged in order to achieve three-phase charging under constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) regimes. During charging, the electromagnetic torque is cancelled and the closed unity power factor is achieved with total harmonic distortion (THD) of grid current below 5% by using the vector proportion integral (VPI) controller. Moreover, balanced current sharing between stator windings under interleaved mode are maintained to avoid the unexpected charging torque production and to deal with the harmonic current at integrated-DC/DC converter side. Furthermore, simulation model of the proposed integrated charger is built and simulated in order to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Investigation of a low speed tubular linear generator with inter-modular permanent magnets
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Wave energy is a source of renewable energy which has demanding and unique requirements on the electrical drive. This paper presents a tubular linear inter-modular permanent magnet generator designed for integration into a wave energy converter. The proposed topology is specifically designed for a low operating speed of 0.5m/sand a magnetic gap of 3mm, characteristics not well-suited for conventional electric machines. The large gap is being driven by a desire to integrate the machine within the wave energy converter to accommodate sealing and encapsulation requirements. It is common for generators intended for wave energy to rely on magnetic gearing, provided by flux switching machines with small pole width magnets on the stator interacting directly with translator teeth. Unfortunately, most topologies of this nature rely on a small magnetic gap, and so are not suitable for a fully integrated design. Bias flux machines, however, have a larger pole width consisting of permanent magnets and the flux modulation is via a toothed stator and toothed translator. The resultant larger stator pole means they are potentially more appropriate for applications with a large magnetic gap. In the structure investigated here, the permanent magnets are embedded between the stator modules, providing cooling vents for efficient PM cooling, better resilience to a large gap and potential savings in the assembly process. Comparisons are made between the proposed generator and two other competing topologies of the same class. The optimized dimensions of the presented linear generators are achieved through a genetic algorithm, targeting an increase in average thrust force and a decrease in force ripple. Utilizing 2D axisymmetric finite element analysis, the generators are simulated under both no-load and full-load conditions, and a comprehensive comparison of the results is provided. Finally, the demagnetization state of the PMs within the proposed topology is discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-objective sequential model predictive control for high-power railway induction motor application
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) has demonstrated its effectiveness in several industrial applications, but it grapples with weighting factor (WF) tuning challenges. This paper presents a comparative analysis between conventional MPC and Sequential MPC (SMPC) for an induction motor driven by a three-level neutral point clamped (3L-NPC) inverter. Unlike classical MPC, the SMPC technique does not incorporate a global cost function. Instead, it employs a cascade of simple cost functions, thereby eliminating WFs. Simulation studies were conducted using parameters of a high-power motor for railway applications, incorporating up to four control objectives. The comparison metric employed is the steady-state total harmonic distortion index, with SMPC prevailing in the majority of scenarios. This outcome signifies the potential of achieving commendable motor performance while circumventing the arduous WF tuning process. Additionally, a parameter variation test was conducted, demonstrating the control’s robustness against such testing conditions.

articleTitle: Optimal design of passive filters for minimization of harmonic distortion in industrial power system applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Harmonic distortion is a serious issue for both industrial customers and power suppliers. Therefore, its reduction is a basic requirement for any power system, to improve stability while complying with acceptable harmonic limits. An optimization method is presented which determines the compensatory values of an optimal passive filter, one which mitigates the harmonic pollution levels of frequency-dependent components in a non-sinusoidal power system, with the objective of maintaining the power factor within desired limits. The objective of the proposed method is to minimize the nonlinear current conditions of industrial customer’s loads and the background voltage distortion from power suppliers at the point of common coupling (PCC). To further enhance the power quality performance, other practical constraints for the total voltage harmonic distortion limits are taken into account in the proposed design, ensuring compliance with IEEE 519-2014 guidance and capacitor loading constraints established in IEEE 18-2012. In addition, the harmonic resonance constraint is formulated to diminishing harmonic resonance risks that may arise from the passive filter connection. The utilization of shunt passive filters is the most widespread method of harmonic mitigation, due to their simplicity, practicality and ease of operational control. Detailed results are provided which validate the performance of the passive filter according to widely used IEEE standards assessments, based on previously published numerical examples of loads in non-sinusoidal conditions.

articleTitle: A decimation approach applied in real-time system identification for DC-AC inverters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: To reduce the computational burden of each interruption set aside to achieve parameter estimation of multiple power conversion architectures, this paper presented a decimation approach that can be employed to estimate coefficients of the transfer functions of multiple single-phase inverters in real-time operation. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the approach in terms of the same estimation accuracy and the same identification speed compared with the conventional way, however, the proposed approach only takes one-third of the computation burden suffered by its conventional counterpart per interruption.

articleTitle: Battery energy discharge optimisation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The uncertainty around recycling of Lithium-Ion batteries and increased focus on sustainability has led to investigations of using second life transportation batteries (used EV/HEV batteries) to provide an energy storage capability. However, the reliability and performance of these batteries are unclear, and each vehicle manufacturer has different specifications for battery chemistry, number and arrangement of battery cells, capacity, voltage and size. It could be useful to be able to connect different batteries from different sources together to obtain a single hybrid second life battery solution with enough power and energy to provide useful grid support. Previous work focused on deriving a theoretical control method from voltage modified Ragone plots to maximise available discharge energy. In this paper, the theory is underpinned by experimentally derived results generated using a multi-modular fault-tolerant cascaded dc-dc converter. Experimental validations are performed on a battery system with constant load to validate the power sharing strategy. The increase between this power sharing strategy and discharging the batteries one at a time is shown to be around 6%.

articleTitle: Sequential direct speed predictive control without weighting factors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Direct speed predictive control (DSPC) provides fast dynamic control with a better disturbance rejection capability but suffers from weighting factor selection. This paper proposes a sequential DSPC without weighting factors for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) control. For this purpose, the sequential weighting factor elimination method is applied to the DSPC method, thereby taking advantage of both the DSPC method and the sequential weighting factor elimination. The proposed system is confirmed through simulation studies under various operating conditions of an electrical drive system. Finally, an enhanced DSPC method with improved control performance and lower design complexity is achieved.

articleTitle: Cooperative control strategy of multi-unit motor based on minimum copper consumption for long stator segmented linear motor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a current cooperative control strategy of multi-unit motor with minimum copper consumption is proposed to improve the efficiency of long stator segment permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM). Firstly, the state equation of the unit motor is established by analysed the motion from the previous stator segment to the next stator segment. Secondly, the coupling factor is designed to describe the change process of the back EMF (electromotive force) during the motion of the motor, and the total thrust expression of the multi-unit motor is obtained. According to the voltage equation of unit motor, the state equation corresponding to the sum of current and the difference of current is obtained, and the corresponding current cooperative controller is designed. The Lagrange equation is designed with the minimum copper consumption as the optimization objective, and the optimal solution is obtained. The effectiveness of the proposed current control strategy is verified byHIL.

articleTitle: Sensorless model predictive direct speed control of an induction motor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Model predictive direct speed control (MPDSC) for an electric motor eliminates the need for a cascade control structure and enhances the disturbance rejection capability of an electric drive. On the other hand, sensorless control reduces the cost of electrical drive systems while enhancing system reliability. To leverage the benefits of both sensorless control and the MPDSC strategy, this paper proposes a sensorless MPDSC-based induction motor (IM) drive. An extended Kalman filter is designed to estimate the states required for the MPDSC strategy and sensorless control. To validate its effectiveness, the proposed electric drive is tested under various operating conditions, including load changes, speed reversal, dynamic speed changes, and parameter inaccuracies. The results confirm its satisfactory control performance. Finally, an advanced IM drive with the advantages of the MPDSC strategy and sensorless control is introduced.

articleTitle: Fast embodiment of a laboratory traction load for an 83 kW electrical motorbike
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper describes the proceedings done to develop a simple and intuitive experimental laboratory traction load to test the energy performance of an 83 kW electric sport motorbike. The traction load platform is basically composed of a wheel-to-road equivalent roller, a gear transmission, an electric break, an inertia flywheel, a load cell to act as dynamometer, a tachometer, powering source and instrumentation electronics for monitoring purposes. The set of components already available at the laboratory, and the necessity of using a cheap dynamometer integrated to an equivalent model to test the electric motorbike at full load in the laboratory, originated the development of this economical solution that electromobility engineers and power electronics practitioners will find attractive to test electric vehicles at their laboratory facility. Description of the traction load embodiment, principle of operation and manufacturing specifications are detailed along this paper towards the test of the 83 kW electric motorbike.

articleTitle: A global optimization method for dual bridge series resonant DC-DC converter based on time domain modelling
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The traditional model of the dual bridge series resonant DC-DC converters (DBSRC) is established based on the fundamental harmonic analysis (FHA), of which the accuracy is low. Thus, there are some control errors and efficiency reduction of the DBSRC. In this paper, the segmental analysis method and the time domain model of the DBSRC is adopted, which can accurately describe the characteristics of the DBSRC. Besides, the reflow power and switching losses will lead to the efficiency reduction of the DBSRC. To optimize the efficiency of the DBSRC, a global optimization method based on extended-phase-shift (EPS) control is proposed. Firstly, the principle of reflow power is analysed, and the optimal model of reflow power is established. Then, the global optimization method is established by combining soft-switching conditions. Finally, the experimental comparison between the proposed method and the traditional method based on FHA is carried out under the wide voltage gain and the full power range. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional FHA, the proposed modelling method has higher accuracy, and the proposed optimization method can effectively reduce the reflow power, significantly reduce the switching losses, and greatly improve the transmission efficiency of the DBSRC.

articleTitle: Intelligent green public transport in border cities
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: An intelligent green public transportation system is proposed to improve urban mobility and increase sustainability in cross-border regions. Integration of the new system with upgraded infrastructure is expected to reduce travel time, thus enhancing mobility options and supporting Vulnerable-to-Exclusion (VTE) groups, such as elderly and students. The new system is also expected to promote energy efficiency thus strengthening network sustainability in the cross-border regions. The new integrated cross-border system will support work and school trips in Western Macedonia Region of Greece (Florina and Prespes Municipalities), and Pelagonia Region of North Macedonia (Bitola and Resen Municipalities).

articleTitle: Design study on hybrid excitation flux switching motor for electric taxiing system in aircraft
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an electric motor design for an electric taxiing system in aircraft. Electric motors for the electric taxiing system require high power density and high mechanical robustness of rotor. A hybrid excitation flux switching motor as a kind of variable flux motors is a good candidate because all active components such as permanent magnets and windings are located on the stator body essentially suitable for high speed rotation. An optimum design study on hybrid excitation flux switching motor is conducted based on finite element analysis using multi-objective genetic algorithm. For the design study, aluminum conductors for windings are introduced and a use of local non-magnetization technique for rotor electrical steel sheets are assumed to improve the power density and the rotor mechanical strength. Besides, the iron loss of rotor made of high-tensile electrical steel sheets is evaluated because an increase in iron loss is one of concerns with the high-tensile electrical steel sheets. The optimum design results based on finite element analysis show that both the power density with reduced rotor weight and the rotor mechanical stress using locally non-magnetized rotor high-tensile electrical steel sheets meet for the requirements.

articleTitle: Successive approximation based phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Most grid-connected converters are configured in grid following (GFL) mode where they are designed to follow the grid voltage and inject a current specific to the required power. GFL requires phase-locked loops (PLLs) to monitor the phase angle and amplitude of the fundamental component of the grid voltage. PLLs need to be fast and should have a low computational burden to prevent delays in tracking the voltage and to ensure the accuracy of the angle to maintain synchronism. Various PLLs have been extensively discussed in the literature and this paper discusses and demonstrates a novel Successive Approximation PLL (SA PLL). The new SA PLL does not require any control parameters. It uses measured grid AC voltages and with an initial set of estimates for grid angle (θ), it successively calculatesVd andVq adjustingθuntilVq equals zero. Simulations have demonstrated that it has a fast dynamic performance, low computational burden and can react stably to harmonics and unbalance in the grid voltage, giving comparable performance to a well-tuned DSOGI-PLL.

articleTitle: Junction temperature monitoring of power devices using convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The temperature-sensitive electrical parameter-based method (TSEP) enables non-invasive and accurate junction temperature (T j) monitoring of power devices. However, most TSEPs are challenged by the load current and device aging, and consequently suffer from degraded performance ofT jmonitoring. To address this, aT jmonitoring method based on an optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) model is proposed to exclude the effect of load current and device aging. In this method, the turn-on collector current (I C) is selected as the TSEP, and the temperature characteristics of the turn-onI Care thoroughly analyzed by mathematical modelling. Moreover, the parameter dependence of the turn-onI Cis fully investigated with the extensive double-pulse tests. Then, with the aid of the CNN, the adverse effects of load current are mitigated. Finally, experimental verification is given to prove the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed model based on a single-phase rectifier.

articleTitle: Traction force ripple caused by electromagnetic parameter asymmetry analysis of A 12/13-pole linear flux-switching permanent magnet motor designed for urban rail transit
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic parameter asymmetry (EMPA) of a 12/13-pole linear flux-switching permanent magnet motor (LFSPM) has been investigated. The objective of this paper is to analyse the traction force ripple caused by asymmetric electromagnetic parameters by means of mathematical derivation and finite-element analysis (FEA). Finally, it is proved that the harmonics of the traction force ripple caused by EMPA of the studied 12/13-pole LFSPM is all at lower order and the order number is no more than four.

articleTitle: Three-level DC-DC converter with fuzzy logic-based MPPT controller for photovoltaic applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a fuzzy logic-based controller designed for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in a high-gain dc-dc three-level boost converter (TLBC) specifically tailored for photovoltaic applications. High-gain dc-dc converters, exemplified by the three-level converter, prove advantageous in photovoltaic systems by facilitating the elevation of low PV voltages to higher levels, thereby mitigating power losses and enhancing overall efficiency. The advantages connected with the use of fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs) include a reduction in the demand for advanced mathematical modeling, allowing for real-time operation through computational efficiency. Such features can lead to heightened efficiency, dependability, and scalability in addressing nonlinear problems, particularly within power converter-based systems. The simulations done using MATLAB/Simulink show that the proposed fuzzy logic-based MPPT provides high, robust behavior with minimised steady- state error under fast-varying environmental situations compared with traditional MPPT algorithms.

articleTitle: Analysis of conducted EMI for dual active bridge DC-DC converter in an electric traction application
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Dual active bridge (DAB) converters are commonly used in power conversion applications with switching devices that operate at high frequencies and high switching speeds. There can be current ringing (oscillation) both in the collector of the switching devices and in the transformer due to the high dv/dt and the parasitics in the transformer and the switching devices. This paper analyses the main causes of common-mode and differential-mode conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) by focusing on the high dv/dt, high switching frequency, the dominant parasitics of the switching device, and the transformer. Based on the simulations, the parasitics and non-linearity behaviour of the switching devices, and transformer parasitics are the main causes of the conducted EMI. In addition, increasing the switching frequency increases both the power loss and conducted EMI because the parasitic capacitances become dominant at high frequencies. To quantify the influences of the parasitic capacitances and the nonlinear behaviour of the switching device, both time domain and frequency domain analysis for the sources of the conduced EMI and some mitigation techniques using Saber<sup>®</sup>simulator is presented. On top of that, the effect of the transformer magnetising inductance on soft switching is studied.

articleTitle: Design and development of high voltage DC power supply for remotely operated vehicle applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This research is dedicated to the design and development of a specialised high voltage DC (HVDC) power supply tailored for Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) applications, placing a specific emphasis on undersea drilling environments. Traditional HVDC systems for ROV drilling applications are characterised by large size, high costs, and low efficiency, often necessitating extensive components such as large transformers, 12 to 48 pulse rectifiers, and meticulous attention to thermal management. In response to these challenges, our study proposes a power supply system that integrates a 6-pulse rectifier and a Multilevel Boost Converter (MBC). The primary objective is to deliver a compact and integrated power supply solution that optimizes power conversion efficiency and fulfils the unique requirements of ROVs operating at 5000 V. Simulation results conducted through PLECS software validate the functionality of the proposed system. The outcomes demonstrate its capacity to generate a high-amplitude DC voltage with minimal ripples, positioning it as a viable and efficient solution for ROV applications. The efficiency considerations indicate the potential for achieving efficiency levels exceeding 95% at high loads, marking a significant improvement compared to conventional HVDC systems. This research contributes to advancing power supply solutions for ROVs, addressing challenges associated with size, cost, and efficiency in undersea drilling environments.

articleTitle: The effect of winding configuration on the performance of six-phase segmented switch reluctance motor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper the effect of winding configuration on the performance of six-phase Segmented Switch Reluctance Motor (SSRM) in terms of iron losses, torque profile, and efficiency is investigated. A circuit-coupled Finite Element (FE) model is developed to accurately consider the switching condition and control circuit of the six-phase SSRM and ensure a fair comparison between configurations. In the switching control system, the effect of the Initial Firing Angle (IFA) and Conduction Period (CP) on the performance of different winding configurations are investigated. Then, the overall performance of different winding configurations at their optimum IFA and CP combination are compared. The results indicate that the N-S winding configuration has a superior performance compared to other topologies.

articleTitle: Cascaded control for PMSG currents and speed without knowledge of mechanical quantities
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The present paper addresses the control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (PMSG). The system is based on the cascaded control of stator currents through an inner control loop, with speed regulated by an outer one. The control of currents is based on proportional-integral (PI) regulators. Speed control is based on the method of Mechanical Quantities Variation Dependence-Less Control (MQVD). That enables overcoming the limitations of recent control strategies, as they rely on the mechanical characteristics of the system. That enhances the system's response to variations in the mentioned characteristics. The viability of the proposed control system is validated through simulations conducted on a 5 kW rated Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Weighting factor-free direct speed predictive control with improved transient performance
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Direct predictive speed control (DSPC) of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) offers a non-cascaded control scheme with a fast dynamic response and better disturbance rejection ability. However, similar to other direct model predictive control schemes, it involves a cumbersome weighting factor selection procedure. This paper proposes a weighting factor-free DSPC scheme with improved transient performance for PMSM control. The proposed method uses a Euclidean norm-based decision-making method to eliminate weighting factors and an additional toque control term to regulate the control performance during transients. Comparative simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method retains the advantages of the traditional Euclidean norm-based decision-making method while enhancing transient performance. Finally, a DSPC scheme with superior control performance and lower design complexity is achieved through simple manipulation.

articleTitle: Analytical model for magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic characteristics analysis of permanent magnet synchronous motor with toroidal winding stator and sinusoidal Halbach array rotor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical model for the rapid examination of the magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic characteristics of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) featuring a toroidal winding stator (TWS) and a sinusoidal Halbach array rotor (SHAR). The analytical model for magnetic field distribution is established by solving the governing Laplace’s and Poisson’s equations of the vector magnetic potential. The no-load magnetic field distribution from SHAR and the magnetic field induced from the armature reaction are individually analyzed. According to superposition theory, the complete magnetic field distribution is derived. Furthermore, an analytical model for motor electromagnetic characteristics, including motor inductances, electromagnetic torque, and motor on-load induced voltage, is formulated. Lastly, the precision of the analytical model is verified through finite element analysis (FEA) simulations across various operational points.

articleTitle: Dead-time and forward-voltage compensation for IGBT and MOSFET half-bridge voltage-source inverters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a feed-forward compensation method of dead time and non-linear forward voltages of half-bridge voltage-source inverters, equipped with either IGBTs or (SiC) MOSFETs, is laid out, simulated and experimentally verified. These specific non-idealities are compensated by modifying the PWM-based modulator, for every switching period, while taking into account a (possibly) significant current ripple. The only measurement needed is the output current. Furthermore, this compensation is unique to the semiconductor technology, considering different values for both the switch and diode characteristics. Finally, this compensation could be easily extended to two-level converter topologies using multiple half bridges, resulting in unique compensation per leg.

articleTitle: A model-free predictive current control method for segmented PMLSM
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The phase inductance of segmented linear motor is unbalanced, and the dynamic disturbance cannot be ignored for back electromotive force (EMF) when the mover enters and exits the stator segment. At the same time, the current and thrust control become more difficult because of the mismatch of the model parameters. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a current control strategy based on model-free predictive current control (MFPCC). A hyperlocal model of dual three-phase permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM) with stator segment is constructed. A predictive current controller is designed based on the deadbeat principle, and a disturbance observer is designed to compensate the effects of unbalance inductance, dynamic disturbance of back EMF and parameter mismatch. Finally, it is verified by experiments that MFPCC can effectively weaken the influence of unbalanced inductance, and suppress the disturbance of back EMF and parameter mismatch. The proposed method improves the robustness and current tracking performance, and thrust fluctuation is reduced.

articleTitle: Physics-and data-based random conductance AC arc model
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Arcs occur frequently in aviation electrical systems, and can lead to fires. Therefore, it is important to diagnose and eliminate arc in a short time. Since most arc models cannot reflect arc’s random noise, this paper principally derives the random conductance AC arc model (RCAAM) based on the simplified Schavemaker model (S-SM), along with the even-order harmonics and high-frequency harmonics data of arc noise. The derived random-conductance AC arc model (RCAAM) is compared with the simplified Schavemaker model (S-SM) and experimental data in frequency domain. The result shows that the RCAAM can reflect an arc’s harmonics accurately.

articleTitle: Dual-winding permanent magnet synchronous motor system based on carrier phase-shift PWM torque ripple suppression effect analysis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: High order current harmonics in PWM drive system will affect the performance of permanent magnet synchronous motor, resulting in motor torque pulsation and vibration; In order to harness the degree of freedom brought by the double-winding permanent magnet synchronous motor system for more intricate motor control, the paper proposes carrier phase-shift modulation technology, which significantly reduces the output torque ripple of the dual-winding permanent magnet synchronous motor system by exploiting the current harmonic offset of the topology of two inverters. Additionally, the paper discusses the application of MTPA (Maximum Torque Per Ampere) and Field weakening Control in dual-winding motor systems, integrating them with carrier phase-shift modulation for motor system control. The suppression effects in low-speed and high-speed regions are validated through finite element simulation. Finally, experimental verification of this suppression method is conducted using the StarSim hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) semi-physical motor simulation platform.

articleTitle: Discrete state-space simulation of a three-phase diode rectifier input
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: In industry there are countless numbers of modelling software packages designed to achieve tasks relating to design of all aspects of engineering. Despite this the end user of the product may not necessarily have access to such software or the expertise to use it or interpret the results. The rectifier at the input to industrial equipment is non-linear, and so the input currents and their effect on the supply at the point of common connection cannot be calculated using a closed-form solution. This paper details the use of discrete state-space modelling to simulate the front end of an electric drive and how it interacts with the grid. This data can be used to estimate impact on harmonic content of the input current waveforms and determine whether certain choices will conform to standards. Since this is uses fundamental circuit analysis it does not require additional toolboxes or libraries and could be embedded into a software application and given to customers. The model produces practically identical results to the Simscape electrical toolbox.

articleTitle: Analysis of cooling structure of axial flux permanent-magnet synchronous motor for electric aircrafts
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The axial flux permanent-magnet synchronous motors (AFPMSM) received intensive attention for electric aircraft applications. In an effort to further reduce the temperature rise, volume and mass of the motors, three water-cooling structures are proposed in this paper, including the annular spiral structure, the radial spiral structure and the parallel structure. The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations are carried out to compare their fluid and thermal performance. The velocity, pressure and temperature distribution of the cooling medium, as well as the temperature distribution of AFPMSM, are also analysed, with the consideration of the influence from the water pumps used in the cooling structures. The results demonstrated that the parallel water-cooling structure performs better than the other two structures under most conditions.

articleTitle: A new robust design method of a hairpin winding permanent magnet motor with high solving efficiency
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a new robust design method for permanent magnet motors with high solving efficiency. Firstly, a hybrid population-based intelligent algorithm with a sequential solving strategy is proposed to transform the robust optimization problem into a deterministic optimization and robust analysis problem. The manufacturing uncertainties of PM height, PM width, PM position, and PM remanence are considered. In addition, the support vector regression method is adopted to construct an approximate model to improve the efficiency of robust design. To illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a hairpin winding permanent magnet motor is designed and prototyped, and the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and simulation results are verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Detection of winding fault for PMSM using 1D-CNN
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The research on winding fault diagnosis of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) has received great attention from scholars in recent years. However, most current research requires manual feature extraction, which places high demands on researchers’ prior knowledge, signal processing theory and practical experience. Base on this, this paper proposes a diagnosis method for winding faults in the PMSM using 1D convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). Firstly, the harmonic components of the zero-sequence voltage signal between the neutral points of the three-phase windings and the resistance network are analysed. Secondly, the experimental data of the zero-sequence voltage under different operation states and winding conditions are collected. After pre-processed by data normalizing and segmenting, the 80% databases are used to train and validate the fault diagnosis model using 1D-CNN for zero-sequence voltage signal treatment, and the remained databases are applied to test the generalization performance of the fault diagnosis model. The proposed method can achieve winding fault diagnosis of the PMSM under variable speed and load states in high accuracy without the requirement of extracting fault features manually.

articleTitle: Dynamic characterisation of a linearised transfer function of non-ideal buck converters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The inherent nonlinear behaviour of DC-DC power supplies complicates the task of working out their linear models, which are essential for a model-oriented control. In a model-oriented control design approach, the accuracy of the plant model directly influences the performance of the control system as the plant parameters tend to be linked to the gains of the controllers. This paper presents a dynamic analytical model of a DC-DC buck converter based on small signal analysis with a closed loop control. The small signal model is used to analyse the small deviations around the steady-state operating point of a buck converter leading to an accurate modelling of the closed loop converter parameters. A complete state-space analysis is undertaken where the output voltage to duty ratio transfer function for a non-ideal buck converter including the parasitic elements is developed.

articleTitle: A simple online arithmetic computational method for efficient operation of PM-based motors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: PM-based motors, due to their high efficiency have received discernable attention in EVs and drives. Operating a PM machine in the constant torque region requires the Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) trajectory to be followed to get maximum operational efficiency. This paper presents a simple arithmetic computational method for current reference generation in the FOC of an IPMSM. Non-linearity and cascaded complex computations for determining the stator current and the quadrature current references in conventional methods can be avoided with the proposed method. The proposed simple iterative approach will reduce the computational burden and processing time.

articleTitle: Matrix converter based compensator for unbalance mitigation in traction system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Modern AC electric trains are designed as single-phase loads and are operated on the three-phase utility grid which causes load asymmetry and leads to unbalanced current ﬂow in the three-phase grid. Several traction unbalance compensators have been proposed in literature. However, most of them include a large DC link capacitor, which is notorious for its high rate of failure. This paper presents the topology and the control algorithm of a matrix converter based traction unbalance compensator. The proposed topology does not incorporate any DC link capacitor and therefore is very reliable compared to several compensators proposed in literature. The eﬃcacy of the proposed compensator is demonstrated by simulation in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Optimized modular multilevel converter topology using Si/SiC hybrid half-bridge submodule
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) has emerged as a promising solution for medium and high-voltage power conversion applications. This paper proposes a modified configuration of the MMC model based on a conventional half-bridge submodule (HBSM) utilizing a Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET hybrid approach. The combination of Si IGBTs and SiC MOSFETs offers a great advantage of employing the low cost and high voltage capability of Si IGBTs along with the faster switching speeds and low power loss of SiC MOSFETs. A hybrid HBSM places the Si IGBTs on the upper side and SiC MOSFETs on the lower side in order to reduce the switching and conduction power losses. This arrangement of the hybrid system for MMC cells enables improvements in the converter’s performance and efficiency. A nine-level voltage of MMC (9LMMC) model based on IGBT/SiC hybrid HBSMs is simulated using the PLECS<sup>®</sup>Standalone tool to verify the effectiveness of the modified converter topology.

articleTitle: Hollowed windings for an improved cooling of permanent magnet electrical machines
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Thermal management is of paramount importance in permanent magnets machines designed for e-mobility, as magnets may lose their properties in high temperatures environments. It is therefore vital to cool down the machine thoroughly to maintain the system efficiency. The integration of advanced electrical windings (like hairpin conductors) in new generation of electric engines improves the filling factor and enables larger current densities. However, these higher values of current densities magnify the thermal management constraints. We fabricated the hollowed hairpin structures by LPBF (laser-powder-bed-fusion) 3D printing using an AlSi7Mg powder (d50 ~10µm). The use of a cooling fluid flow through the hollowed structures helps to better cool down the conductors and consequently the system. By realizing a numerical analysis, we studied the impact of the channels geometry to maintain the temperature below 85°C. For a Reynolds number of 500, the ratio of fluid cross section to total channel cross section should be set in the range between 30-35% to maximize heat extraction and may allow for an increase of the electrical current up to 71% (compared to plain conductors). Experiments demonstrates that the use of hollowed channels improved the heat losses extraction.

articleTitle: Modelling and control development for a hybrid microgrid system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The paper presents the modelling and control development for a hybrid microgrid system involving both DC and AC sub-grids. First, by using manufacturing data, a hybrid microgrid model including a PV system, a battery energy storage system (ESS), and a biogas generator sharing a DC bus and connecting to AC sub-grid via a grid tied inverter could be obtained. Then, control development for each individual microgrid component is implemented. Finally, a high-level controller for maintaining the DC and AC sub-grid operations of the hybrid microgrid could be achieved. In the DC sub-grid side, DC voltage level is maintained by the battery ESS and the bio-gas generator whereas the PV power generation is maximized via maximum power point track (MPPT) control. In the AC sub-grid side, the AC bus is defined by the main grid under the grid supporting/following operation or by controlling the grid tied inverter under the grid forming operation. The hybrid microgrid is developed and validated by Simscap-based Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: An ANN-wavelet based distribution transformer protection
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Transformers are crucial components in electrical power systems, serving as vital links for efficient energy transmission and distribution. With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources and the need for enhanced grid resilience, hybrid transformers have emerged as a promising solution. Combining the benefits of traditional transformers with modern technologies, hybrid transformers offer improved performance, reduced environmental impact, and advanced functionalities. However, this technological advancement also calls for equally advanced protection mechanisms to ensure their reliable and safe operation. In this paper, artificial neural network based approach is used to protect a two-winding transformer in laboratory environment. Feature vectors are differential currents and experimental studies cover energizing, sympathetic inrush currents, and internal faults. Simulation and real times experiments show that the proposed hybrid transformer protection scheme is able to detect normal and faulty conditions.

articleTitle: Dual polarity multi-level boost DC-DC converter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: With the shift in focus to DC collection networks, for renewable applications, comes the opportunity to explore the potential of DC links for bipolar DC collection networks. These networks provide greater transmission efficiency compared to their AC counterpart and do not require frequency or phase matching techniques. While DC links for unipolar networks have been realised within the literature, there has been limited focus on DC links that are compatible with bipolar networks. With their inherent cable redundancy, bipolar collection networks are an attractive option for renewable applications where cables are difficult to access. A demonstration unit of a scalable bipolar DC-DC converter is presented and experimentally validated. The unit utilised the combination of 2N-1 and inverting 2N Cockcroft Walton topologies in tandem, as this design facilitates a simultaneous positive and negative output, that operates with a single switch. The similar designs of the 2N-1 and 2N topologies enable balanced voltage output, minimising the need for voltage-balancing techniques. The efficiency of the demonstration unit was shown to be 98 % during steady-state operation.

articleTitle: A DC/DC converter for centralized energy storage in HVDC applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Energy storage systems (ESS) are often used to face grids stability problems, providing ancillary services. This paper introduces a modular converter to integrate a massive ESS built of supercapacitors to an HVDC link. This approach stores a big amount of energy in a single ESS, unlike other proposals that distribute the stored energy in series-connected submodules. The topology consists of two branches of half-bridge and full-bridge submodules. Due to the nature of the ESS, the converter must be able to handle with large voltage fluctuations on one side, from zero-voltage to full-charge (in the range of hundreds of kilovolts), and constant voltage on the other side (also in the range of hundreds of kilovolts). A control strategy is proposed, and simulations using average arm models demonstrate that the proposed converter satisfies the requirements, remaining stable and following the references as desired.

articleTitle: An optimized control strategy using multivariable modulation and reactive power exchange cancellation for a multi-active bridge (MAB) converter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: A multi-active bridge (MAB) converter is an interesting energy hub topology that has emerged in recent years. This multi-port structure has recently attracted a lot of attention, especially for applications soliciting renewable energy sources and energy storage systems. In general, the main objective of controlling a MAB converter is to manage the active power flows between its ports based on each port's requirements. However, optimizing the control of this converter can be achieved by adding another constraint, aiming to minimize the system’s losses for example. In this paper, a novel optimized control strategy is proposed for a MAB converter consisting of any number of ports. This approach provides users with a choice between prioritising efficient system operation, which may result in the loss of soft switching at specific switches, or aiming for soft switching at all system switches with decreased losses, even if it leads to suboptimal efficiency. A 1KW 4-port MAB prototype is built and experimental results are provided in this paper to validate the developed theoretical study.

articleTitle: A versatile and low-cost approach to power electronics practical training
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Electrical machines, power electronics, and electric drives have permeated several industrial sectors with applications spanning across electrical and mechanical engineering, automotive, aerospace, renewable energy, etc. As such, there is an increasing demand for engineers with a skill set in power electronics, machines and drives. In electrical engineering education and specifically in the power electronics field, practical training is a key requirement to train a high-calibre power electronic engineer with skills that satisfies industry needs and employer expectations. In this work, a group from the University of Sheffield introduces a universal power electronics board that is versatile and compact. The proposed board is highly modular and emulates a graduate experience in industry settings. The board provides practical power electronics education resources to address industry needs and minimise cost to higher education institutions whilst enabling scalability in practical teaching, allowing more students to benefit from this type of training. The proposed system also addresses learning outcomes at levels 3, 4 and 5 for vocational qualifications, covering both the basics of power electronics and more advanced application-level concepts.

articleTitle: Novel converter-dynamic voltage restorer integration to mitigate voltage sags
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Voltage sag is common power quality issue that disturb load operation and need attention. The Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) is an effective solution for voltage sags compensation. However, the conventional DVR, consisting of a DC source and an inverter, is utilised only during voltage sag events, which raises economic feasibility concerns. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates the DVR with the power converter with the aim of mitigating grid voltage sags that the converter may encounter. The proposed method involves combining the DVR directly with the converter, eliminating the need for a DC source and a separate DC-AC inverter within the DVR. Such an integration provides a cost-effective and efficient solution for voltage sag mitigation. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated by simulation studies, demonstrating its reasonability and its capability to compensate for voltage sags. The results highlight the potential advantages of this integrated system in ensuring uninterrupted converter operation.

articleTitle: Investigation of alternative magnet configurations in a biased-flux machine
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Biased flux motors are a type of electric machine which operate in an unconventional manner but can offer structural and performance advantages over more conventional topologies. Achieving a suitable design in this relatively uncommon topology requires identifying the effect of various factors on their performance. Even small changes in the structure and magnet configuration can have a significant impact on performance. In this paper, the magnet configuration, flux barriers, and bridges are investigated to try and improve the performance of a base-line biased-flux motor. The details of the structure and operating principles are explained and structures are optimized for torque production in a fixed volume. The no-load and full-load operations of alternative variants is studied in terms of cogging torque, flux density, flux line, torque profiles, and over-load capability. Moreover, a complete comparison has been made between split magnet and single magnet topologies in an inter-modular permanent magnet motor. The magnetic stresses on the PMs are studied to assess the demagnetization risks. It is been explained how splitting the magnets and the introduction of flux barriers increases the torque density and flux bridges decrease the demagnetization risk.

articleTitle: An integrated approach for optimisation of electric drivetrain noise including manufacturing tolerances
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: With the desire to minimise the number of prototypes build during drivetrain development, increasing reliance is being put on simulation as a design tool. Integrated workflows that integrate various tools enable better understanding of which design metrics have the highest impact on drivetrain targets, and minimise delays due to various teams waiting for the output from colleagues in other departments. When two industry standard tools are integrated and can be operated using one interface invaluable insight can be acquired. This paper demonstrates a coupled workflow to evaluate noise due to electric vehicle traction motors; this workflow allows the analyst to identify the best design from the noise, vibration and harshness perspective but also easily evaluate how sensitive it is to manufacturing accuracy.

articleTitle: Ageing parameter detection for condition monitoring of SiC MOSFET based drives
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The recent advancement in semiconductor technology has allowed for the development of a new type of device, based on Silicon-Carbide (SiC). Most industries especially the automotive sector are keen on utilising these devices within their products, due to their lower losses and higher switching frequency, during operation. These SiC devices are in an infant stage and so must be investigated further to establish their reliability and expected lifetime. Failure modes of the devices are typically dependent upon the package of the MOSFET. The most common package is TO247 and from the previous studies, it is noted that the main failures for TO247 package MOSFETs are located at the bond wire, die attach, and baseplate to substrate layer. This is due to the difference in the hardness of materials i.e. SiC and Copper. This work tests a TO247 packaged SiC MOSFET (SCTW100N120G2AG) via an Active Power Cycling Test (PCT) to determine the failure mechanism and the remaining useful life. Two measurements are taken: the rise in junction temperature above ambient temperature (const. △T<sub>j</sub>) and the constant heating current (const. I<sub>heat.</sub>). Three samples are tested until the failure, which is defined as the point at which the V<sub>ds-on</sub>has increased by 10% of its rated value. X-ray computing tomography (XCT) of the samples is also performed to understand the reason for failures, revealing that the cracking at the bond wire interface is the reason for the increased R<sub>ds-on</sub>. This is due to the mismatch in the coefficient of thermal expansion between the Bondwire and the Direct copper bonding (DBC). Threshold Voltage V<sub>th</sub>has increased by 12% as well due to the ageing of the SiC MOSFET which indicates slight degradation of the gate oxide layer.

articleTitle: Using surface mounted resistor for power module switching current measurement
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach of using surface mount resistor (SMR) for measuring switching current in power module applications. To overcome the challenge of the SMR parasitic inductance on measurement results, the SMR impedance is characterised first and used to compensate the switching current measurement results. To validate the approach, a SiC-MOSFET half-bridge circuit is built and both Rogowski coil and SMR are used to measure the switching current. The switching current measured by SMR using our proposed approach shows agreement with the results obtained by Rogowski coil. The measurement error without using our proposed approach is quantified, and illustrates that our proposed approach helps to reduce the measurement error. Thus, it provides a compact switching current measurement solution by comparing with state-of-the-art current measurement approaches, which shows that it is promising for future highly integrated wide bandgap power module application.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Neimark-Sacker bifurcation in DC chopper fed DC drives via the Monodromy matrix
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The nominal behaviour of a DC chopper fed DC drive under proportional integral (PI) control is a periodic orbit whose period equals that of the clock. But as some controller parameters are varied, this nominal orbit loses stability via a Neimark-Sacker bifurcation leading to the birth of a quasi periodic orbit (the so called torus) with a considerable impact on the losses and lifetime of the system. Further variation of the system parameters leads to several period-adding, phase-locking and chaotic phenomena as the torus breaks down. In this paper, by employing the Monodromy matrix, we were able to determine analytically when this occurs, and hence appropriate action can be taken when the controller is designed. Analytical and numerical results validate our findings.

articleTitle: Optimized model predictive control with reduced switching states for neutral point clamped converters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The implementation of multilevel converters, particularly the neutral-point clamped (NPC) converter, has risen in modern power electronics owing to its ability to enhance power quality and voltage levels. Model predictive control (MPC) has emerged as an important strategy in NPC converter control, offering empowerment in managing multiple objectives with rapid dynamic responses. However, conventional MPC suffers from computational burdens, delaying its practical implementation. This paper proposes a reduced switching states MPC (RSS-MPC) approach for NPC converters, significantly reducing computational time by segmenting the prediction horizon into discrete zones with fewer potential switching states. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving control objectives, maintaining robustness against disturbances, and variations in grid voltage, thereby presenting a promising solution for practical implementation in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of the effect of friction on the efficiency calculations of an electric machine for a wave energy converter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Wave energy is a source of renewable energy that is reaching commercial reality. The low-speed, high torque oscillating motion and a desire for direct drive power take off favours the development of large radius magnetically geared generators. Lifetime cost of energy is a key performance indicator of the technology and is directly proportional to efficiency of power conversion. Friction loss is proportional to the electromagnetic airgap closing force within the electrical machine, meaning optimisation of the generator design and losses experienced in the drive train is a coupled problem. For favourable economics, losses in the electrical machine and lubrication system most both be reduced. This paper describes the development of a direct drive electrical generator and lubrication system for an attenuator wave energy converter. For the first time, the finite element analysis model of a flux reversal machine is coupled to a simplified tribology model to investigate the relationship between electrical machine design and bearing loss. An objective function is used to optimise the mechanical drive train for maximum annual energy yield for a specific wave energy converter in a known wave resource. It is shown that integrating the bearing losses into the objective function of an optimisation routine influences the final electrical machine design by putting a focus on mass reduction. Furthermore, the bearing loss is shown to decrease system efficiency by 1.1%.

articleTitle: Flow field analysis of a high torque electric machine integrated with power electronics - a numerical study
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Demand for high-torque electric machines is growing in different applications, which requires the development of more powerful electric machines, which in turn needs more effective cooling systems. In this study, the design and improvement of an air-cooling system for a 3 MW high-torque electric machine with integrated power electronics has been investigated by numerical simulations. The whole machine was modelled in detail, including converters at both ends. Adjustment of desirable air flow rates for the machine as well as converters was executed by changing the converter outlet hole size. Results show that straight air guides can help air distribution through gaps between laminations as well as the air gap, while using pin vents can increase air flow mixing and stability of laminations. However, both will increase pressure drop. Insulation between laminations and compression plate can also cause significant increase in pressure drop, which cannot be avoided. The air return manifold is another component which raises the total pressure drop and diminishes the air flow rate to the converter. Finally, by determining the optimum outlet hole size, the system curve is provided in a wide range of air flow rates, which will be used in the selection of a suitable fan.

articleTitle: Selective harmonic generation for dielectric barrier discharge reactors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a high voltage waveform generator capable of generating waveforms composed of multiple sinewaves whose frequencies are integer multiples of a fundamental frequency (harmonics). The proposed approach allows synthesis of inverter pulse-trains with a large number of controlled harmonics, called selective harmonic generation. These waveforms are produced with a GaN inverter and tested for their utility in generating ozone in a dielectric barrier discharge reactor, obtaining 193 ppm/W (parts per million per watt) with a 0.5 lpm (litre per minute) flowrate of dry air as the feedstock.

articleTitle: Assessment of two DC voltage droop options for small-signal stability in MMC-based multi-terminal DC grids
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: The paper studies the stability issue in a multi-terminal HVDC grid where multiple vendors implement different control strategies for DC voltage regulation. Small-signal analysis reveals the effects of the droop gain values of two control options, with one showing better robustness than the other. The effects of the response time of the outer control loops as well as those of the DC reactors are also investigated. The results of the small-signal analysis are supported by EMT simulations.

articleTitle: A high-bandwidth current shunt resistor for testing GaN devices
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative method for high bandwidth switching current measurement tailored to the rapid switching speeds of gallium nitride (GaN) devices. Accurately measuring switching currents is crucial for evaluating switching performance. However, high-speed current measurement faces persistent challenges, such as layout inductance interference, limited bandwidth, high costs, and large size and weight. To tackle these challenges, a flux cancellation shunt resistor is proposed which is integrated into the PCB board to improve the power density and to minimize loop parasitic inductance. Additionally, theS-parameters of the proposed current sensor have been analyzed. By capturing the frequency-domain impedance of the proposed current sensor, the bandwidth of the sensor is estimated to be 150 MHz. The experimental double pulse tests conducted using the proposed current sensor and commercial shunt resistor demonstrate its accurate measurement and high bandwidth capability.

articleTitle: Towards harmonic cancellation in motors using selective noise suppression random SVPWM method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Random pulse width modulation techniques are used in AC motors powered by two-level three-phase inverters, which cause a broadband spectrum of voltage, current, and electromagnetic force. The voltage distribution across a wide range of frequencies may increase the vibration and acoustic noise of motors. To solve this problem, this study proposes a selective noise suppression (SNS) method to eliminate voltage harmonics. The general formula of the SNS is derived. In this method, the switching frequency is constant. The pulse position is calculated by the duty cycle of the current switching cycle. Simulation and experimental results show that the method effectively create a spectrum gap at a specific frequency. This study provides a valuable reference for eliminating electromagnetic vibration and acoustic noise at resonant frequencies in motors.

articleTitle: AC copper loss in flat rectangular wire concentrated winding of axial flux machine for high-speed EV drives
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2024)
abstract: Recent advancements in edgewise winding technology now enable the use of flat rectangular wires with significantly high width-to-height ratios greater than 5, which are seldom utilized in electric vehicle (EV) traction drive applications, offering new winding design possibilities for high-speed axial flux machines (AFMs). This paper investigates the application of concentrated edge-wound flat rectangular wire coils in high-speed axial flux machines with the goal to reduce AC copper loss. Particular emphasis is placed on the end winding—a component frequently overlooked in AC copper loss calculation for radial flux machines. Additionally, this study introduces a novel extended 2D-FEM approach, which provides a more computationally efficient assessment of AC copper loss including the end winding part.
